prospects.ai_hook: Ask for Henry (Jessica runs the office - likely who answers). Lead with the commercial permit: he pulled BLDC24-0089 at 2018 Waterfront Dr in IOWA CITY - a commercial roof tear-off and replacement, 60 miles from his Clinton shop. Say: 'you're driving to Iowa City for commercial tear-offs and there's nothing online for anyone to find you by.' Back it with Iowa reg C133608 active and 100% recommend across 19 Facebook reviews. Text-friendly: he invites texts to 563-249-8414. DO NOT mention BBB (not accredited / Not Rated), DO NOT call his Facebook dead (last post July 2025 but it's his only asset and it's at 100%), DO NOT mention that ezroofing.com belongs to a Florida company - that lands as 'you lost your name.' Spell it Fernandez, not the BBB's 'Fernanadez.' Do NOT say 53 reviews - unconfirmed.

Dubuque local - same town as Ricky. Lead with volume and the paperwork: 128 permitted projects on file and an ACTIVE USDOT number with 3 drivers, and the only thing a homeowner searching 'furnace repair Dubuque' can land on is a Facebook page. Say: 'you've pulled 128 permits in this town and I couldn't find a website for you anywhere.' Best proof point: a single job at 2459 Kerper Blvd took four 115k-BTU furnaces and four A/C units - that's commercial-scale work with no site to show it on. DO NOT say anything like 'looks like you're growing fast' - permits are actually DOWN 44 to 31 to 28 across 2023-2025. DO NOT assert his Facebook page is gone; it wouldn't load logged-out, so ask rather than tell. Don't credit the company with decades - the LLC formed Dec 2021.

Ask for Brett Seward, President - he's named on both association profiles and handles bids. Lead with the union credential: they're a Bricklayers Local 8 SIGNATORY in the current 2025 trades directory, and they already OWN sewardmasonryinc.com - it's been serving a blank 'Under Construction' page. Say: 'you already bought the domain, it just says Under Construction.' That's the sharpest opener in this batch - he's paid for it and never got a site. Back it with two association memberships (CIB AGC + SIBA) and commercial/institutional scope: masonry, concrete, air barriers, thermal and moisture protection. DO NOT state a number of years in business - SOS says 2017 but the firm reads older. DO NOT mention the Facebook post honouring 'Joann Seward' - tone is unclear and it could be a memorial. Address is 812 Park St, not the 798 Procore lists.

Home-market call. Ask for Sara, she runs the schedule. Lead with the history: Encyclopedia Dubuque traces Dimmer Brothers through four Dubuque addresses since 1971 - Garfield, Jonathan Lane, East 7th, now Davenport Street - and 55 years later there is still nothing to find online. Say: 'you're in the Encyclopedia Dubuque and you still don't come up on Google.' DO NOT mention licences (a second licence type shows inactive) and DO NOT open with reviews - they have zero reviews anywhere and it is their sore spot.

Ask for Mike Tobin, President. THE KEY MOVE: do NOT say 'you don't have a website' - they BOUGHT tobinbrothers.com and never built on it. Say 'you own tobinbrothers.com and it's sitting empty - I already built what belongs on it.' That is flattering instead of accusatory. Back it with 63 years: shop opened 1 January 1963 on NE Perry, AGC and MIMCA member. Alt number (309) 208-6124. DO NOT raise reviews (they have none) and DO NOT claim anything about their licence - IDPH status was never verified.

ASK FOR JENNIFER BUNJES - she is the named principal. Lead with the mismatch: a union shop bonded for public and private jobs up to $500,000, in the Blue Book since 2000 - and the whole company runs off an @mac.com email address with no domain at all. Say 'you're bidding half-million-dollar work off an @mac.com address.' If the main line is dead try (815) 703-5226. DO NOT name Don Bunjes (unconfirmed), DO NOT mention the Rockford Chamber (their listing lapsed), DO NOT lead with the MBE flag (self-reported), and DO NOT guess at their headcount - no source has one.

Ask for Daniel, he answers himself. Lead with the review wall: 41 reviews at 4.7 and nothing online to send anyone to. Julie H.'s line about the crew working hard and steady all day long is the exact proof a homeowner wants and it is stranded on Google. Dubuque local, so offer to stop by rather than pitching over the phone. Storm and hail work is the seasonal hook: after a hail event the whole tri-state calls at once and whoever is findable gets the volume. Website build is the play. SEO is the day-30 follow-on, not the opener.

Ask for Mark, he opened the doors in March 1994. Highest scoring prospect in the batch. Lead with the property manager angle: one of his reviewers manages 230 units and found him through word of mouth, not search. Multi-unit and commercial is where the recurring money is and it is exactly the buyer who searches before calling. Back it with 4.9 across 43 and an A+ BBB record, both public. Boiler work is a real differentiator, fewer shops every year will touch one. Thirty-two years in one town is the headline. Website build first.

prospects.business_name: Chris Ihrig Lawn Care and Snow Removal LLC
prospects.ai_hook: PHONE-FIRST, he has no Facebook page, so there is no DM path. 118 reviews in Maquoketa and every single one is five stars, which is the whole pitch by itself. Reviewer line worth quoting back: responsible, honest, timely, responds within minutes. Seasonal urgency is real and it is now, get on the route before the first storm is a line he already uses on customers. Maquoketa is wide open, nobody is ranking, so flag him for the SEO upsell at day 30 after the build closes. Do not lead with SEO.

Ask for Gary, family owned and he quotes the jobs himself. Thirty-four years in Springfield with 65 reviews and no website to hold any of it. Seasonal timing works twice a year here: attic top-ups sell in autumn on heating bills and radiant barrier sells in summer on attics that cook. Joe C.'s review leads with the cleanup, which tells you what his customers actually rate him on, so put that on the page. Siding is the natural attach, if it is coming off anyway that is the cheapest moment to deal with what is behind it.

Ask for Justin, he quotes and grinds it himself. 114 reviews at a perfect 5.0 with new ones still landing, which is live proof rather than a stale wall. DO NOT PITCH SEO on this one, Cedar Rapids stump grinding scored 5 out of 20 on winnability. The play is the site plus lead capture: he quotes off a photo and a rough diameter, so a form that takes a photo upload turns his phone time into booked work. Most of his volume is the call after somebody else took the tree down and left the stump. Tight-access backyard work is his differentiator.

Owner Rick Mai, 30 years claimed, phone-first via the Facebook page since there is no site. FLAG: BuildZoom shows license C124995 expired 2020-07-08 with a BZ score of 0, so do not lead with licensing. Sourced from an in-person encounter in Dubuque, still running print classifieds. No contact record in HubSpot yet, create one before dialing.
